meta.title: How the World Uses AI
meta.subtitle: A data-driven report on global generative-AI usage by country, class, occupation, and demographic
meta.method: Synthesized from TWO multi-source, adversarially fact-checked deep-research passes: (1) global usage by country/class/occupation/demographics; (2) a deep dive into the granular question taxonomy, prompt behavior, and sensitive/emotional uses. Combined: 50+ sources fetched, ~230 claims extracted, 33 confirmed by 3-vote adversarial verification. Core findings are vendor first-party usage data (OpenAI/NBER w34255, Anthropic Economic Index & affective-use study) plus independent surveys (Pew, Ipsos, Reuters Institute, Stanford HAI, Microsoft, BCG, Common Sense Media, HBR) and traffic estimates (Similarweb).
meta.key_caveat: Nearly all figures are dated snapshots from 2025-2026. Vendor data is self-reported and platform-specific: Claude skews heavily to developers (coding 34-37%) while consumer ChatGPT coding is only 4.2% — the two paint opposite task pictures because they have different user bases. Gender is name-inferred, not self-reported. Similarweb numbers are modeled web-traffic estimates (exclude apps/API).

income_divide.title: AI adoption tracks income (the digital divide)
income_divide.source: Anthropic Economic Index; Microsoft AI Diffusion Report
facts: A 1% higher GDP per capita is associated with ~0.7% higher Claude usage per capita.
Global North: 24.7% of working-age population used AI tools vs a markedly lower share in the Global South (H2 2025).
Lower-income countries show the fastest growth but the lowest per-capita levels.
Coursework use is more common in lower-income countries; work & personal use dominate in higher-income ones.

youth_share.title: AI is young: nearly half of ChatGPT messages come from under-26s
facts: ~46% of ChatGPT messages come from users aged 18–25.
64% of US teens (13–17) use AI chatbots; ~30% of those use them daily.
Among US teens, ChatGPT leads at 59% — more than double any competitor.
80% of university students now use generative AI (Stanford HAI 2026).

occupation.title: Usage by occupation & context
occupation.source: Anthropic Economic Index; BCG Asia-Pacific (Jul 2025, 4,500+ employees, 9 markets); Stanford HAI
facts: Software/coding is the single largest professional use of Claude (34-37% of conversations).
Writing is the #1 work task on ChatGPT (40% of work messages).
~10% of all ChatGPT messages are tutoring / teaching requests.
In Asia-Pacific, 78% of employees report weekly AI use — above the global average.
Students/coursework = 19% of Claude.ai usage; 80% of university students use genAI.

global_surveys.title: Independent multi-country surveys
global_surveys.source: Reuters Institute; Ipsos AI Monitor 2025; BCG
facts: Weekly genAI use nearly doubled in one year: 18% (2024) → 34% (2025) across 6 countries; ever-used rose 40% → 61% (Reuters Institute, Argentina/Denmark/France/Japan/UK/US).
Ipsos AI Monitor 2025 surveyed 23,216 adults across 30 countries (Mar–Apr 2025); 67% say they understand what AI is.
BCG Asia-Pacific: India leads adoption at 92%; Japan trails at 51%.

granular_taxonomy_pct_of_messages.source: OpenAI/NBER w34255 (some sub-figures read from charts)

deep_dive.writing_note: Two-thirds of all Writing requests are edits/critiques/translations/summaries of user-supplied text; only one-third is novel text. Sub-types by frequency: Editing/Critiquing > Personal Writing > Translation > Argument/Summary > Fiction.

prompt_literacy.source: arXiv 2509.25513 (n=937 US adults, controlled multi-turn experiment; preprint)
prompt_literacy.unmeasured_gaps: Average prompt length, voice-vs-text share, single- vs multi-turn rates, and politeness prevalence are NOT publicly available from primary vendors.

sensitive_emotional.sources: OpenAI/NBER; Anthropic affective-use study (Clio, ~4.5M conversations); Filtered.com/HBR; Common Sense Media
sensitive_emotional.perception_vs_reality: Stated-use rankings (Filtered.com/HBR Zao-Sanders 2025) put 'therapy/companionship' at #1; measured conversation logs show emotional/affective use under 3%.
sensitive_emotional.claude_affective_note: Most affective use is interpersonal advice & coaching, not companionship.
sensitive_emotional.teens: 72% of US teens (13-17) have used an AI companion at least once; over half use companion platforms a few times a month (Common Sense Media 2025). Intense emotional use concentrates on purpose-built apps (Character.AI, Replika), not general assistants.
